messages:
incident-bot: P0: elevated TLS handshake failures on /v1/chat and /v1/generate from multiple regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1). Auto-paging on-call.
emma: acknowledging. dashboards show spike in 502/524 from edge -> clients report \"TLS handshake failed\" in browser console and mobile SDKs.
felix: Im on-call. did we push any certs or ALB changes in the last hour? :mag_right:
emma: cert rotation was performed ~18m ago to replace intermediate and add new cross-signed CA. listener update logged ~11:38UTC.
gina: tailing envoy on edge node: ```
[2026-03-15T11:46:12Z] error "SSL handshake error: EOF during handshake" client=10.10.3.44:53412
[2026-03-15T11:46:12Z] debug "tls: client hello truncated or wrong version"
```
felix: hmm. "truncated" suggests fragmentation or truncated ClientHello; other logs show "certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain" for some clients.
emma: I pulled the cert presented by the ALB with curl -Iv from a linux host:
```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (13.32.11.22) port 443 (#0)
* found 1 certificates in /etc/ssl/certs
* server certificate:
  subject: CN=api.redwood.ai
  start date: Mar 15 11:30:00 2026 GMT
  expire date: Mar 15 11:40:00 2027 GMT
  issuer: CN=Intermediate CA
* SSL certificate verify result: unable to get local issuer certificate (20), continuing anyway.
```
infra-bot: noted: ALB listener is terminating TLS. certificate chain uploaded at 11:38UTC. no other listener changes.
felix: hypotheses:
- H1: incomplete cert chain deployed -> older TLS stacks fail with verify errors
- H2: ClientHello fragmentation due to MTU/MSS -> some handshakes truncated (causing EOF/wrong version)
- H3: ALB TLS negotiation policy incompatible with legacy clients after cert change -> protocol/cipher mismatch
- H4: VPC peering appliance restart / route churn during cert rollout caused intermittent TCP RSTs
gina: starting tcpdump on affected ENI and one ALB subnet. saving pcap to /var/tmp/tls-1792468000.pcap
infra-bot: tcpdump started on eni-02f7 and alb-subnet-b. filter port 443.
felix: quick packet trace (sanitized):
```
11:45:59.001 IP client -> alb TCP 443  MSS 1460  len 1300 (fragmented)
11:45:59.002 IP alb -> client RST
11:45:59.003 IP client retransmit SYN+ (smaller) -> handshake fails
```
emma: that lines up with truncated ClientHello then RST. also saw ALB logs with code \"SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR\" and some entries with HTTP 502 downstream.
infra-bot: peel logs: peering appliance (peer-ap1) had rolling restart at 11:39UTC for config push (related to NAT egress announce).
felix: timeline summary:
- 11:30UTC: new cert issued
- 11:38UTC: cert uploaded and associated with ALB listener
- 11:39UTC: peering appliance rolling restart
- 11:45UTC: first customer errors reported
- 11:50UTC: alert threshold exceeded and P0 page
- 11:58UTC: capture and hypothesis building

felix: mitigation plan proposed:
1) rollback ALB to previous cert bundle that includes full chain (quick) -> expected immediate reduction in verify failures (felix)
2) apply MSS clamping (tcp-mss 1200) on peering gateways to avoid fragmentation on path (infra)
3) if still noisy, flip ALB to TCP passthrough to let backend terminate TLS temporarily (emma)
4) schedule controlled peering restart during maintenance window to reproduce and fix MTU settings (infra)

felix: executing 1) now (console command):
```
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --certificates CertificateArn=arn:aws:acm:...:old-cert
```
felix: rollback applied at 12:03UTC. ALB health checks green.
emma: monitoring: failure rate drops from ~38% -> 10% in ~60s. still seeing edge cases from older Android/iOS devices.
infra-bot: MSS clamp applied to peering gateway pair (rule id clamp-179246). set tcp-mss 1200 on egress path at 12:07UTC.
felix: after MSS clamp, packet traces show fewer fragments; retransmits much reduced. overall client failures drop to <1% by 12:12UTC.
gina: collecting artifacts for RCA: envoy logs, ALB access logs, pcap snippets, peering appliance restart logs, OpenSSL s_client outputs from affected device emulators.
felix: in-thread hypothesis status:
- H1 (incomplete chain): confirmed -> high confidence (rollback strongly correlated with drop)
- H2 (fragmentation/MTU): confirmed -> medium/high confidence (MSS clamp mitigated)
- H3 (policy mismatch): unlikely -> low confidence (no evidence; modern clients fine)
- H4 (peering restart impact): possible contributing factor -> medium confidence (restart timing overlaps)
sre-bot: incident labeled tls-handshake, state -> mitigated -> monitoring. SLA impacted for ~42m. postmortem due in 48h.
emma: immediate followups:
- felix: re-upload cert with full chain and perform multi-vantage verification in CI before listener swap (include old TLS stacks)
- infra: add MSS/clamp monitoring to peering health checks and document safe MTU range
- ops: send customer-facing status update summarizing root cause and mitigation
- gina: attach logs and packet captures to incident doc and map affected customer IDs
felix: adding runbook note: after cert rotation, run `openssl s_client -connect $ALB:443 -showcerts -tls1_2` from a matrix of vantage points (linux, mac, Android emu, old openssl) and verify chain + handshake.
emma: Ill draft the postmortem and assign action items. thanks for quick responses. tagging @felix @gina @hank @infra-bot.
